parameters.content:
## RAG Knowledge Assistant (n8n + Google Gemini)
**Chat page:** `/webhook/rag-chat` with three modes: `?kb=client` (website bot), `?kb=staff` (internal assistant), `?kb=doc&d=<token>` (uploaded PDF)
**1. Index:** open `/webhook/rag-reindex-CHANGE-ME-4` (keep private) after editing **Knowledge Base Documents**. Docs are split by section and embedded with `gemini-embedding-001` (768 dims); vectors are stored in workflow static data.
**2. Upload:** `/form/rag-upload` extracts PDF text, splits it by page, embeds it and redirects to the chat. Uploads expire after 24 h (max 5 kept).
**3. Ask:** `/webhook/rag-ask` checks rate limits (20 per IP per 10 min, 400 per day), embeds the question, ranks passages by cosine similarity, and Gemini writes an answer that cites passage numbers. Only cited passages are returned as sources.
Swap the static-data store for Pinecone, Qdrant or Supabase (pgvector) for large document sets.

parameters.jsCode:
// Code node: "Knowledge Base Documents"
// Edit or add documents here, then open the re-index URL to rebuild the vectors.
const docs = [
 {
  "kb": "client",
  "docId": "client-01",
  "title": "services",
  "text": "# Services

## About Harborline Software
Harborline Software is a small software house with 18 people: engineers, designers, QA and project managers. The team works from Karachi and remotely, and serves clients in the US, UK, Europe and the Gulf. The company was founded in 2019 and focuses on practical automation and AI for small and mid-sized businesses. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 19:00 Pakistan time (PKT, UTC+5), with overlap hours for US and UK clients.

## AI chatbots and knowledge assistants
We build chatbots that answer questions from a company's own documents: help-centre articles, policies, product manuals, PDFs and websites. This approach is called RAG (retrieval-augmented generation). The bot finds the most relevant passages first and then writes an answer based only on them, with links to the sources. Typical uses are website support bots, internal staff assistants and sales assistants. We can connect the bot to a website widget, WhatsApp, Slack or Microsoft Teams. We work with OpenAI, Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude models, and with vector databases such as Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase (pgvector) and PostgreSQL.

## Workflow automation with n8n
We design and build business automations in n8n, including self-hosted n8n on the client's own server. Common projects: lead capture and CRM updates, invoice and document processing, email and Slack alerts, reporting, approvals, and syncing data between tools such as HubSpot, Google Sheets, Airtable, Shopify and QuickBooks. We also migrate automations from Zapier or Make to n8n to cut monthly costs.

## Web applications
We build custom web apps and internal tools: client portals, admin dashboards, booking systems and SaaS products. Our main stack is React and Next.js on the front end and Node.js or Python (FastAPI) on the back end, with PostgreSQL as the database.

## Mobile apps
We build cross-platform mobile apps for iOS and Android with React Native. Mobile projects usually start at 8 weeks because of app store review and device testing.

## Maintenance and support
After launch we offer monthly support plans that cover bug fixes, small changes, monitoring, security updates and backups. See the pricing document for plan details.

## What we do not do
We do not take on crypto trading bots, gambling products, adult content, scraping that breaks a website's terms, or projects that collect personal data without consent. We also do not do SEO link building or social media management.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "client",
  "docId": "client-02",
  "title": "pricing",
  "text": "# Pricing and payment

## Hourly rate
Our standard rate is $45 per hour for development, design and project management. Discovery calls are free and last 30 minutes.

## Fixed-price packages
Most clients choose a fixed-price package so the budget is clear up front.
- AI chatbot (RAG) Starter: $450. One knowledge base of up to 50 pages, a website chat widget and source links. Delivered in about 7 working days.
- AI chatbot (RAG) Standard: $900. Up to 300 pages, two channels (for example website and WhatsApp), conversation logs and a handoff to a human. About 12 working days.
- AI chatbot (RAG) Advanced: $1,800. Multiple knowledge bases, user roles, an admin panel to upload documents, analytics and a CRM integration. About 20 working days.
- n8n automation Starter: $300 for one workflow with up to 3 connected apps. Standard: $600 for up to 3 workflows. Advanced: $1,200 for up to 6 workflows with error handling and monitoring.
- Web applications and mobile apps are quoted after a discovery call. Typical small web apps cost $3,000 to $8,000.

## What changes the price
The main factors are the number of integrations, the amount and quality of the source documents, custom design work, user roles and permissions, and the deadline. Rush delivery (about 40% faster) adds 25% to the price.

## Payment terms
Projects under $1,000 are paid 50% up front and 50% on delivery. Larger projects are split into milestones, with a 30% deposit and the rest paid as each milestone is approved. We accept bank transfer, Wise, Payoneer and card payments, and we can also work through Upwork contracts. Invoices are due within 7 days.

## AI usage costs
The client pays the AI provider (for example OpenAI or Google) and hosting costs directly, on their own account, so they keep full control. For a typical support bot these costs are usually between $5 and $40 per month, depending on traffic.

## Discounts
Registered non-profits and education institutions get 10% off. Returning clients get 5% off their next project. We do not offer free trials of custom work, but we can build a small paid proof of concept first.

## Refunds
If we have not started work, the deposit is refunded in full. After work has started, completed milestones are not refundable, but you keep all the work delivered so far.

## Support plans
- Basic: $150 per month. Bug fixes, security updates and monitoring, with replies within 2 working days.
- Growth: $350 per month. Everything in Basic plus up to 8 hours of changes each month and replies within 1 working day.
- Priority: $700 per month. Everything in Growth plus up to 20 hours of changes, same-day replies and a monthly review call.
Unused hours do not roll over. Plans can be cancelled with 30 days' notice.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "client",
  "docId": "client-03",
  "title": "process",
  "text": "# How we work

## Step 1: Discovery call
A free 30-minute video call to understand your goals, users, current tools and budget. You can book it through the project enquiry form on our website. After the call we send a short summary of what we understood.

## Step 2: Proposal
Within 2 working days of the call we send a written proposal with the scope, timeline, milestones, price and payment terms. Proposals are valid for 14 days.

## Step 3: Kickoff
Once the proposal is accepted and the deposit is paid, we hold a kickoff call, set up a shared Slack or WhatsApp channel and give you access to the project board. You get one named project manager as your main contact.

## Step 4: Build and weekly demos
We work in one-week sprints. Every week you get a short demo (live or recorded) and a written update: what was done, what is next and any decisions we need from you. You can test work in progress on a staging link.

## Step 5: Testing and launch
Our QA team tests on real devices and browsers before launch. For chatbots we test with a set of real questions and share the results with you. We then launch together with you, usually early in the week so we can watch it closely.

## Step 6: Handover and warranty
At handover you get the source code, logins, documentation and a recorded walkthrough. Every project includes a 30-day warranty: any bug in the agreed scope that appears within 30 days of launch is fixed for free. After that you can move to a monthly support plan.

## Timelines
Small automations take 3 to 7 working days. Chatbot packages take 7 to 20 working days. Web apps usually take 6 to 12 weeks and mobile apps 8 to 14 weeks. The biggest cause of delay is waiting for content, access or feedback, so we agree response times at kickoff.

## Changes to scope
Small changes are fine. If a change adds more than about 2 hours of work, we send a short change request with the extra cost and time for you to approve before we do it.

## Communication
We reply to messages within one working day, usually much faster. We can hold calls in your morning or evening, including US Eastern and UK hours. All calls are in English.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "client",
  "docId": "client-04",
  "title": "faq",
  "text": "# Frequently asked questions

## Who owns the code?
You do. Once the final payment is made, you own all the code, designs and documents we created for your project. We only keep the right to reuse general know-how and open-source components.

## Will you sign an NDA?
Yes. We are happy to sign your NDA before the discovery call, or we can send our standard mutual NDA.

## Is my data safe?
We only use the access you give us for your project. Logins are stored in a password manager, never in chat or email. We use separate accounts per client, turn on two-factor authentication and remove our access at the end of the project if you ask. For AI chatbots we can use providers and settings that do not train on your data.

## Can the chatbot give wrong answers?
A RAG chatbot answers only from your documents and shows its sources, which greatly reduces made-up answers. When the documents do not contain the answer, the bot is set up to say so and offer a human contact instead of guessing. We also review real conversations during the first weeks and improve the documents or settings.

## Can you host it for us?
Yes. We can host on your cloud account (DigitalOcean, AWS, Google Cloud or Azure) so you stay in control, or on our managed server for a monthly fee. Self-hosting n8n typically costs $6 to $24 per month in server fees.

## Do you work with our time zone?
Yes. Most of our clients are in the US, UK, Europe or the Gulf. We keep at least 3 hours of overlap with your working day and can join calls outside our office hours when needed.

## Can you work with our existing developers?
Yes. We often join existing teams, follow their Git workflow and code review process, and hand over to their developers at the end.

## Do you offer a free sample?
We do not build custom work for free, but the discovery call and the written proposal are free. For larger projects we suggest a small paid proof of concept first.

## How do I get started?
Fill in the project enquiry form on our website. You will instantly see a rough estimate, and we will contact you within one working day to book a discovery call.

## What languages can the chatbot speak?
Our chatbots can answer in English, Arabic, Urdu, Spanish, French, German and most other major languages, even if the documents are only in English.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "staff",
  "docId": "staff-01",
  "title": "handbook",
  "text": "# Employee handbook

## Working hours
Normal working hours are Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 19:00 Pakistan time, including a one-hour break. Core hours are 11:00 to 16:00: everyone must be reachable on Slack during core hours unless they are on approved leave. Team members on US-facing projects may shift their day to 13:00 to 22:00 with their project manager's agreement.

## Hybrid and remote work
The office in Karachi is open every weekday. Engineering, design and QA staff work from the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays and may work remotely on the other days. Sales and operations staff work from the office Monday to Thursday. Fully remote arrangements need written approval from the CEO. Working from another city or country for more than 5 working days needs approval from your manager at least one week in advance.

## Attendance
Check in on the #attendance Slack channel when you start and finish work. If you will be more than 30 minutes late, tell your manager before 10:30. Three unexplained late starts in a month are discussed in your next one-to-one.

## Equipment
Every employee gets a company laptop, a second monitor for the office and a headset. Laptops must use full-disk encryption and the company password manager. Report lost or stolen equipment to operations within 24 hours. Equipment is returned on your last working day.

## Allowances and expenses
Remote-working staff receive an internet allowance of PKR 5,000 per month, paid with salary. Work expenses such as client meetings, software approved by your manager or travel must be submitted through the expenses form within 30 days with a receipt. Expenses above PKR 25,000 need approval before you spend the money.

## Salary and payroll
Salaries are paid on the last working day of each month by bank transfer. Payslips are sent by email. Annual salary reviews take place in January, based on the performance review.

## Learning budget
Each employee has a learning budget of $300 per year for courses, books, certifications or conference tickets. Ask your manager before buying, and share what you learned in a short team session.

## Code of conduct
Treat colleagues and clients with respect. Harassment, discrimination and bullying are not tolerated. Report concerns to your manager or directly to the CEO; reports are handled confidentially. Do not discuss client names or projects on social media without permission.

## Contacts
- Leave and attendance questions: your team lead, then operations.
- Payroll and expenses: the operations manager.
- IT access and equipment: the #it-help Slack channel.
- Anything else, or if you are unsure: your manager.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "staff",
  "docId": "staff-02",
  "title": "leave-policy",
  "text": "# Leave policy

## Types of leave
- Annual leave: 14 working days per calendar year, for holidays and personal time.
- Sick leave: 8 working days per year, fully paid.
- Casual leave: 6 working days per year, for short personal matters such as family events or errands.
- Unpaid leave: available when paid leave is used up, with your manager's approval.
- Work from home: extra remote days outside the normal hybrid schedule, requested the same way as leave.
Public holidays announced by the Government of Pakistan are paid holidays and do not count against your leave.

## How to request leave
Submit every request, including sick leave and work from home, through the leave request form on the company portal. Choose the leave type and the start and end dates, and name the colleague who will cover your work. The form counts working days (Monday to Friday) automatically. Your manager approves or rejects the request on the approvals page, and you can see the status in the #leave Slack channel.

## Notice periods
- Annual leave of 1 to 2 days: at least 3 working days' notice.
- Annual leave of 3 days or more: at least 2 weeks' notice.
- Annual leave of more than 10 working days in a row needs CEO approval.
- Casual leave: at least 1 working day's notice when possible.
- Work from home: by 18:00 the day before.
Requests during client launches or the last two weeks of December may be refused if too many people from one team are already off.

## Sick leave
If you are sick, message your manager before 10:30 and submit the leave form when you are able to. For sick leave of more than 2 days in a row, a doctor's note is required.

## Carry-over
Up to 5 unused annual leave days can be carried over into the next year and must be used by 31 March. Sick and casual leave do not carry over and are not paid out.

## Leave during probation
During the 3-month probation period, employees earn annual leave at about 1 day per month but can use sick and casual leave from day one.

## Leaving the company
Unused annual leave for the current year is paid out in the final salary. Leave taken beyond what was earned is deducted from the final salary.

## Maternity and paternity leave
Maternity leave is 12 weeks, fully paid. Paternity leave is 10 working days, fully paid, to be taken within 3 months of the birth. Tell operations as early as you can so we can plan cover.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "staff",
  "docId": "staff-03",
  "title": "engineering-sop",
  "text": "# Engineering standard operating procedures

## Source control
All code lives in the company GitHub organisation. The main branch is protected. Create a branch for each task named type/ticket-short-description, for example feature/HL-142-invoice-export or fix/HL-151-login-redirect. Write commit messages in the imperative, such as "Add CSV export to invoices". Never commit secrets, API keys or client data.

## Pull requests and code review
Open a pull request as soon as the work is ready for review, with a short description, screenshots for UI changes and testing notes. Every pull request needs at least one approval from another engineer, and two approvals for changes to payments, authentication or database migrations. Reviewers should respond within one working day. Use squash merge. The author merges after approval and after the automated checks pass.

## Environments and deployment
Each project has three environments: local, staging and production. Every merge to main deploys to staging automatically. Production releases happen Monday to Thursday before 16:00 PKT; no production releases on Fridays or the day before a public holiday unless it is an urgent fix approved by the tech lead. Tag every production release and write release notes in the project channel.

## Secrets and credentials
Store all passwords, API keys and client logins in the company password manager in the correct client vault. Never paste secrets into Slack, email, tickets or code. Use environment variables for secrets in applications. If a secret is exposed, tell the tech lead immediately and rotate it the same day.

## n8n and automation projects
Build n8n workflows on the staging instance first. Name every node clearly, add a sticky note that explains what the workflow does, and add an error workflow that alerts the #alerts channel. Export the final workflow JSON to the project repository. Credentials in n8n must belong to the client's own accounts wherever possible.

## AI and chatbot projects
Keep a test set of at least 30 real questions with expected answers for every chatbot and run it before each release. Chatbots must show sources and must say when they do not know the answer. Do not send client documents to AI providers that train on customer data. Log conversations only when the client has agreed and their privacy policy covers it.

## Incidents
If a production system is down or giving wrong results, post in #incidents with the client, the problem and when it started, and tag the tech lead. The project manager informs the client within 1 hour. After the fix, write a short incident report within 2 working days: what happened, why, and what we changed to prevent it.

## Estimating
Estimate tasks in hours, not days. Add 20% for testing and review. If a task will take more than 1.5 times the estimate, tell the project manager as soon as you know.
"
 },
 {
  "kb": "staff",
  "docId": "staff-04",
  "title": "onboarding",
  "text": "# Onboarding and performance

## First day
On your first day you receive your laptop, company email, Slack, GitHub and password manager accounts. Operations walks you through the office, the handbook and the leave policy. You are introduced to your onboarding buddy, an experienced colleague who answers everyday questions during your first month.

## First week checklist
- Set up two-factor authentication on email, Slack, GitHub and the password manager.
- Read the employee handbook, leave policy and engineering SOPs.
- Set up the development environment using the project's README and run the project locally.
- Complete one small starter task and open your first pull request.
- Have a one-to-one with your manager to agree goals for the first 3 months.

## Probation
The probation period is 3 months. During probation the notice period is 2 weeks from either side. At the end of probation your manager holds a review; if it goes well you are confirmed in writing, and the notice period becomes 1 month.

## One-to-ones
Every employee has a 30-minute one-to-one with their manager every two weeks to talk about work, blockers, growth and wellbeing. You set the agenda.

## Performance reviews
Performance reviews happen twice a year, in June and December. They cover delivery, quality, teamwork, client communication and growth. The December review feeds into the January salary review. Promotions can be proposed at either review.

## Career levels
Engineering levels are Junior, Mid-level, Senior and Lead. Moving up is based on the scope of work you can own on your own, the quality of your work and how much you help others, not only on years of experience.

## Leaving the company
After probation the notice period is 1 month. Hand over your work with written notes, return all equipment on your last day, and operations will remove your access. You receive an experience letter with your final salary.
"
 }
];
return docs.map((d) => ({ json: d }));

parameters.formDescription: Upload a text-based PDF (up to about 30 pages). It will be split into passages, indexed with Google Gemini embeddings and opened in the chat. Uploads are deleted automatically after 24 hours, so please don't upload confidential documents.
